text.p: Property developer Somprasong Land Plc confirmed on Wednesday that it had failed to meet the interest payment obligation on its Euroconvertible bond.
The payment had been due on Tuesday.
Somprasong said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand that its payment default could be attributed to a prolonged slump of the Thai property market.
It said independent appraisers would be commissioned by the company's management to assess its assets and liabilities.

Somprasong said the planned review of its assets is the first step toward restructuring the company's assets in consultation with its creditors and holders of its $80 million Euroconvertible debentures.
It told the bourse that Bankers Trust would arrange an assets and liabilities restructuring meeting with holders of its bond.

"When all the information is gathered, the company will discuss with Bankers Trustee concerning the proposal on restructuring its capital and liabilities, and call for an extraordinary meeting among debenture holders," it said.
Somprasong's defaulted $3.1 million interest payment had been due since January 21 but the company had obtained a 14-day grace period ending Tuesday to honour the obligation.
It said in the statement that it will not sell off its assets or do anything to affect its debenture holders when the restructuring plan is approved by its creditors.
